comparator.name: Computing Science
components: Cyber Security is the first listed OER specialization; only one 12-EC track is selected.
Restricted selection of one permitted academic minor of at least 15 EC; no optional minor is represented as compulsory.
Genuinely open second/third-year choice of assessable bachelor-level courses.
Required 12 EC individual research thesis, approved in advance. Entry: at least 120 programme EC including the complete first year. Research Methods is recommended, not an additional hard condition.

core: Programming, software design and testing of computational systems
Algorithms, formal reasoning, discrete mathematics and computing systems
Data analysis, machine learning and quantitative modelling in computing
Computer networks, information systems, security and digital responsibility
adjacent: Cyber Security as a formal specialist track in cryptography, web and operating-system security
Data Science as a formal track in machine learning and large-scale data
questions: How can designed software and data tools address real client and societal problems responsibly?

alternatives.label: Computing, data and AI foundations
alternatives.concept: Combines programming, software construction, algorithms, networks and operating systems, databases and discrete mathematics with data science, AI and mathematical methods. Statistical research supports empirical evaluation; AI ethics and business analysis examine concrete societal consequences of computing. It retains substantial computing study while leaving differences in processor architecture, formal language and verification theory, specialist security and a required independent thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The scheduled curriculum contains a sustained programming, algorithms, systems, mathematics, data and AI sequence plus explicitly applied research and societal analysis; the label avoids promising cybersecurity specialisation.

candidates.label: Specialist Cyber Security
candidates.reason: UCR has networks, operating systems and broad AI ethics but no courses in cryptography, web security, operating-system security or penetration testing; replacing the specialist track with adjacent material would not yield a defensible distinct 24-course programme.

candidates.label: Processor and hardware architecture
candidates.reason: Networks and operating-system software does not establish processor/hardware design. No complete distinct hardware programme is supported by the actual UCR catalogue.

routeSelection.basis: The generic Computing Science target does not identify a track. The current adopted OER lists Cyber Security, Software Science and Data Science as three equally formal 12-EC options without designating a general track. Its first-listed track is selected as a neutral tie-break, not for UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The core programme already implements the available software, mathematical and data directions. A second genuinely different cybersecurity programme would require cryptography, operating-system security, web-security and penetration-testing courses absent from the UCR workbook; swapping in adjacent law or ethics courses would misrepresent this specialist direction.

blocks: Both develop sets, relations, propositional and predicate logic, induction and mathematical proof. Radboud also specifies number theory; UCR adds formal game and process modelling.
Both study data structures, asymptotic efficiency, algorithm design and graph algorithms. UCR also introduces computability, reductions and complexity classes.
Both analyse asymptotic algorithmic complexity. UCR develops algebraic algorithms and optimisation; Radboud additionally gives a dedicated treatment of complexity classes and NP-completeness.
Both develop calculus and mathematical problem-solving. UCR extends to differential-equation modelling and Mathematica; Radboud additionally includes probability.
Both develop linear systems, matrix operations, vector spaces, linear maps and eigenvalues. UCR extends to orthogonality, least squares and singular-value decomposition.
Discrete mathematics and graph algorithms are already placed elsewhere; no separate selected course establishes the dedicated counting and recurrence sequence.
No additional selected UCR course is placed at this distinct component; related contributions are already represented once at their strongest counterpart.
Selected discrete mathematics is placed at Mathematical Structures. Radboud’s additional applied logic includes specification, natural deduction and proof-assistant work.
UCR algorithms includes computability and Turing machines, but is already placed at Algorithms and Data Structures. No second course establishes the full dedicated computability sequence.
General logic and functional programming do not establish the dedicated operational/axiomatic semantics and correctness sequence.
General number-theoretic algorithms do not constitute the dedicated modern cryptography sequence.

Both study processes, threads, concurrency, synchronisation and memory management. UCR combines operating systems with network protocols and experimental investigations; Radboud additionally requires separate network-security study.

Both study relational databases, their theoretical basis and SQL implementation. Radboud additionally develops conceptual information modelling; UCR’s description does not establish an identical modelling project.

Both teach functional programming with Haskell, including functions, recursion and types. UCR divides its course between Haskell and object-oriented C++ development, testing and software quality; it is not the full dedicated Radboud sequence.

Both develop structured programming, control flow, functions, recursion and data structures. UCR uses Python and includes object orientation; Radboud uses Rust and adds its own algorithms and complexity sequence.
AI ethics and network/operating-system foundations are not a substitute for the dedicated introductory computer-security sequence.

Python object orientation and C++ classes occur in the selected programming courses, already placed at imperative and functional programming. No additional course reproduces the dedicated Java object-oriented design sequence.
Selected software/networking courses and available robot-motion/control work do not establish CPU circuitry, machine code and processor architecture.

Software design and testing occur in UCR Software Development, already placed once. No additional selected course reproduces the specific stakeholder, requirements and interactive-system design project.
The new required course’s entry/participation conditions remain unverified; general AI methods do not establish specific AI-assisted software development training.
C++ memory management is not the dedicated C/machine-code vulnerability and exploitation course.
The new required course’s entry/participation conditions remain unverified; no selected course establishes a dedicated human-computer interaction curriculum.
The new required course’s entry/participation conditions remain unverified; databases and data handling do not by themselves establish the specific information-retrieval course.
No additional selected UCR course is placed at this distinct component; related contributions are already represented once at their strongest counterpart.

UCR Networks and Operating Systems is placed at operating-system concepts. The additional Radboud course includes mandatory networking/security laboratories and attack/defence projects, which are not independently reproduced.
Selected algorithmic and network work does not establish dedicated OpenMP, MPI and CUDA parallel programming.
UCR Software Development contains design and testing but is placed at its direct Haskell counterpart. Radboud’s additional software-company project with real clients is not separately reproduced.
General operating-system mechanisms do not establish dedicated Linux threats, boot/authentication, malware and sandbox security study.
General programming, SQL and network protocols do not establish dedicated web vulnerability exploitation and mitigation.

Both develop academic skills, study reflection and personal direction. UCR also includes academic writing and civic engagement; Radboud maintains a computing-specific portfolio and mentorship sequence.

Both develop research questions, design, ethical inquiry and reliable evidence. UCR includes empirical data collection and statistical analysis; Radboud gives specific attention to computing research, user studies and stakeholders.
Both address reasoning under uncertainty in intelligent systems. UCR develops probabilistic models and decision theory; Radboud also surveys search, machine learning and social aspects.
Both use R to explore and visualise data. UCR develops data cleaning, transformation and text/spatial workflows; Radboud additionally specifies introductory statistical inference.
Programming assignments contribute project practice, but no separate selected course is placed at this first-year integrated R&D project.

Required12EC individual research thesis with supervisor, formal report and presentations. Scheduled UCR methods and programming projects do not establish its completion; optional independent research is separate from the scheduled180EC.

Both critically examine how computing technologies affect society and institutions. UCR focuses on AI’s business, economic, labour and governance consequences; Radboud also develops philosophical questions about privacy, politics and knowledge.
AI ethics addresses privacy but not the specific legal argumentation, GDPR and human-rights course.
AI’s societal effects do not independently establish the dedicated sustainable-computing sequence.
Genuine15EC minor selection, subject to approval and excluded-overlap rules. It has no predetermined subject counterpart.
Genuine12EC open assessable bachelor-level electives have no predetermined subject counterpart.

notes.text: Both curricula contain programming, algorithms, data analysis and computing systems. Radboud also requires a formal Cyber Security track with cryptography, operating-system and web security, broader formal-computing theory, and an independent Computing Science thesis. UCR cannot present its networks, AI ethics or other courses as substitutes for those specialist requirements.

audience.programmeDescription: Computing Science studies how software and computing systems are designed, implemented and analysed. Radboud combines programming, algorithms, mathematical foundations, information systems and security with independent research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The adopted curriculum allocates180EC, but entry and participation conditions for three newly compulsory courses remain unverified. Relevant UCR computing, mathematics, data and AI study has been assessed provisionally. A final comparison is withheld until those external conditions can be checked.

curriculum.routeLabel: Cyber Security track; entry verification pending
curriculum.limitation: The adopted allocation totals 180 EC: 129 EC core, a 12-EC Cyber Security track, a 15-EC minor, 12 EC of open electives and a 12-EC thesis. The language assessment requires participation, not a passing result; writing skills are integrated into existing credits.
